title: MySQL 8.4 Online DDL Operations
engineering_principles: DDL cost differs per operation; INSTANT has row-version and table-type limits.
practical_examples: Adding a foreign key in place requires foreign_key_checks disabled; dropping a primary key alone requires COPY.
why_it_matters: Gives the operation-level matrix needed to judge migration locking on MySQL.
notes: Read via WebFetch model summary; paraphrased, re-check details against the page. Covers MySQL 8.4; page also cites a 255 row-version limit as of 9.1.0.

title: MySQL 8.4 SHOW REPLICA STATUS
engineering_principles: Seconds_Behind_Source is an approximation; waiting on a GTID set is the documented way to wait for a known write.
practical_examples: WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET returns 0 on success and 1 on timeout; semisync acknowledges relay-log receipt, not apply.
why_it_matters: Shows which MySQL lag signals are unreliable and which mechanisms exist for read-your-writes.
notes: Read via WebFetch model summary; paraphrased, re-check details against the page. Covers 8.4. Supporting pages opened: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/gtid-functions.html ; https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/replication-semisync.html ; https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/group-replication-configuring-consistency-guarantees.html ; https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/group-replication-system-variables.html (default BEFORE_ON_PRIMARY_FAILOVER). No page uses the term read-your-writes as prescriptive guidance.

title: MySQL 8.4 Restrictions and Limitations on Partitioning
engineering_principles: Partitioned InnoDB tables cannot participate in foreign keys on either side.
practical_examples: A CREATE or ALTER that would combine partitioning and foreign keys is rejected.
why_it_matters: Forces a choice between declarative referential integrity and partitioning on MySQL.
notes: Read via WebFetch model summary; paraphrased, re-check details against the page. Covers 8.4.

title: MySQL 8.4 DATE, DATETIME, and TIMESTAMP Types
engineering_principles: TIMESTAMP converts through the session time zone; DATETIME is stored as written.
practical_examples: A TIMESTAMP read under a different session time zone returns a different value than was stored.
why_it_matters: Determines instant versus wall-clock semantics for MySQL columns.
notes: Read via WebFetch model summary; paraphrased, re-check details against the page. Covers 8.4. Time zone support page not opened.

title: MySQL 8.4 CREATE INDEX Statement
engineering_principles: A UNIQUE index permits multiple NULLs on nullable columns.
practical_examples: Functional key parts are allowed in UNIQUE indexes but not in primary keys or foreign keys.
why_it_matters: Needed for cross-engine comparison of NULL behaviour in uniqueness.
notes: Read via WebFetch model summary; paraphrased, re-check details against the page. Covers 8.4.

title: MySQL 8.4 GRANT Statement
engineering_principles: Column-level privileges exist; the GRANT page lists no row-level privilege.
practical_examples: GRANT SELECT (col1), INSERT (col1, col2) ON mydb.mytbl.
why_it_matters: Clarifies which access granularity MySQL documents natively.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Log-Shipping Standby Servers
engineering_principles: Replication is asynchronous by default; remote_apply waits for replay on synchronous standbys.
practical_examples: Setting synchronous_commit to remote_apply for load balancing with causal consistency, at much larger commit delay.
why_it_matters: Primary source for read-your-writes options on PostgreSQL standbys.

title: PostgreSQL 12 Release Notes
engineering_principles: Foreign keys may reference partitioned tables since version 12; unique keys must include all partition key columns.
practical_examples: Detaching a partition takes a SHARE lock on tables referencing the partitioned table.
why_it_matters: Establishes when referenced-side support arrived and the key constraint it depends on.
notes: Text extracted directly with curl. practical_examples: AT TIME ZONE applied twice to convert UTC datetime2 values to datetimeoffset across DST changes.
why_it_matters: Defines SQL Server instant and offset semantics.

title: Unique constraints and check constraints
engineering_principles: A UNIQUE constraint allows only one NULL per column; CREATE TABLE grammar shows no deferrable option.
practical_examples: Filters cannot be applied to UNIQUE constraints but can be applied to indexes with the UNIQUE property.
why_it_matters: SQL Server NULL uniqueness differs from MySQL and Oracle, and deferred checking is not in its grammar.
notes: Read via WebFetch model summary; paraphrased, re-check details against the page. Applies to SQL Server 2017 onward and Azure SQL.
